name: vector-store-qdrant
description: Point knowledge vector search at your own Qdrant instead of the built-in sqlite-vec index. Chunk vectors are written to Qdrant as documents are ingested, and Qdrant answers the vector half of hybrid retrieval — FTS5 keyword search, the graph arm and RRF fusion are unchanged. Your documents stay in PersonalClaw's own database; Qdrant holds vectors and chunk ids only. Enable it to bind it; disable it and retrieval returns to the built-in index.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: Qdrant URL
x-meta.help: Where your Qdrant is listening. The default is a Qdrant running on this machine (docker run -p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant). Pointing at your server IS this app, so it stays on the first screen.

x-meta.label: Collection
x-meta.help: The Qdrant collection to hold chunk vectors. Created on first use with the dimension of whatever embedding model you have bound. Use a fresh name rather than an existing collection — this app deletes and rewrites the points it owns.

x-meta.label: Local folder (no server)
x-meta.help: Run Qdrant's engine in-process over a local folder instead of connecting to a server — nothing to install, good for trying this out. Wins over the URL when set. Single-process only: the folder is locked, so the gateway must be the only reader.

x-meta.label: Timeout (seconds)
x-meta.help: How long to wait on a Qdrant call before giving up. A timeout makes the vector arm contribute nothing for that query; keyword and graph results are unaffected.
